value.microspecies_note: Ferroheme a monoanion: Fe(II) held inside the porphyrin macrocycle by four Fe-N bonds in one connected fragment (no disconnected Fe ion), the propionate on the formyl-bearing pyrrole ring PROTONATED and the propionate on the neighboring ring DEPROTONATED. Which of the two propionates carries the proton is arbitrary; the two are chemically near-equivalent and the SI gives no site-resolved value, so the choice is documented rather than justified. RDKit 2026.03.6 CalcMolFormula returns C49H55FeN4O6- and GetFormalCharge returns -1: the formula matches the GEM's exactly, the charge does NOT. The GEM's -3 is not reachable by any protonation state. The Fe(II)-porphyrinate core is charge-neutral (Fe2+ plus macrocycle dianion), so for this family charge = -(56 - nH): nH=56 gives 0 (both propionic acids, ChEBI:24479, C49H56FeN4O6), nH=55 gives -1 (this species), nH=54 gives -2 (ferroheme a(2-), CHEBI:61715, C49H54FeN4O6). No microspecies has C49H55FeN4O6 with charge -3, and none was written with a disconnected Fe or a formal-charge trick to manufacture one. Derivation and the proposed correction are in `notes`. The dianion is the dominant species at the pipeline's pH 7.2 (propionate pKa near 4.8) and is the same string with the protonated propionate written as [O-]: [H]C(=O)C1=C(CCC(=O)[O-])C2=[N]3C1=Cc1c(C)c([C@@H](O)CC/C=C(\C)CC/C=C(\C)CCC=C(C)C)c4[n]1[Fe]31[N]3=C(C=c5c(C)c(CCC(=O)[O-])c([n]51)=C2)C(C=C)=C(C)C3=C4 (C49H54FeN4O6, charge -2, InChIKey ZGGYGTCPXNDTRV-YRJWGCQVSA-J). Both strings parse in RDKit AND in OpenBabel, which matters because OpenBabel is what eQuilibrator reads with and it rejects RDKit's dative-bond spelling (`<-`, `->`); keep the plain-bond ChEBI spelling. The InChI and InChIKey are the standard ones, in which the metal is always disconnected; they were generated by breaking the four Fe-N bonds and setting Fe to +2, a procedure validated by its reproducing PubChem CID 146026556's key for the dianion character for character.

decomposition_check.error: equilibrator_assets.group_decompose.GroupDecompositionError: Unable to decompose <openbabel.openbabel.OBMol ...> into groups. Five atoms are left unassigned, atomic numbers [26, 7, 6, 7, 6]: the iron, two of the four macrocycle nitrogens and two ring carbons. The same failure with the same five unassigned atoms occurs for all three microspecies (neutral, monoanion, dianion) and for the Fe-free BiGG cache structure the pipeline currently reaches, so it is the Fe-porphyrin core that component contribution has no group for, not the protonation state and not the missing iron. Called as generate_compound.create_compound does, GroupDecomposer().Decompose(Molecule.FromSmiles(smiles), ignore_protonations=False, raise_exception=True), under ~/miniconda3/envs/equilibrator-ext/bin/python; ignore_protonations=True fails identically. The LocalCompoundCache.get_compounds route that thermo_structure_attempt.py uses could NOT be exercised in that environment: it returns status 'failed' with method 'read-only' because cxcalc is not installed, which is an environment limitation and not a verdict on the structure. The decisive test is the direct decomposer call above, which is the same function create_compound invokes at generate_compound.py:119.

notes:
WHAT WAS FOUND. An Fe-coordinated heme a structure exists and is curated in two independent databases: CHEBI:61715 `ferroheme a(2-)` and PubChem CID 146026556 `Ferroheme a(2-)`, which agree on C49H54FeN4O6, charge -2, InChIKey ZGGYGTCPXNDTRV-YRJWGCQVSA-J. The GEM's own annotations reach neither: CHEBI:24479 has no structure at all, and every BiGG and PubChem SMILES writes the iron as a disconnected `.[Fe+2]` (or, in the GEM's yml, a disconnected and formally zero-valent `.[Fe]`), which is why the eQuilibrator cache holds only the iron-free macrocycle and the pipeline's heavy-atom composition check rejects it. The record's SMILES keeps the iron inside one connected fragment with four Fe-N bonds and passes that check.

THE CHARGE COULD NOT BE MATCHED, AND THE GEM IS WRONG, NOT THE STRUCTURE. The task asked for formula C49H55FeN4O6 AND charge -3. The formula is matched exactly; the charge is -1 and no honest structure gives -3. The Fe(II)-porphyrinate core is charge-neutral, so across the whole microspecies family charge = -(56 - nH), giving (C49H56FeN4O6, 0), (C49H55FeN4O6, -1) and (C49H54FeN4O6, -2) and nothing else. Three independent lines say the GEM's pair is an artifact rather than an unusual species. First, the GEM's own SMILES for s_0811 reads in RDKit as C49H56FeN4O6 charge -2, agreeing with neither its declared formula nor its declared charge. Second, the sibling heme o (s_0812, C49H56FeN4O5, -2) IS exactly ferroheme o(2-), the correctly deprotonated ferrous dianion, so the model's convention is the dianion and heme a is the odd one out. Third, EC 1.17.99.9 writes the reaction as Fe(II)-heme o + 2 A + H2O = Fe(II)-heme a + 2 AH2, so substrate and product are in the same iron oxidation state and heme a must be the ferrous dianion too.

PROPOSED CORRECTION (needs a human decision, do not apply silently). s_0811, s_3714 and s_4332 should be formula C49H54FeN4O6, charge -2, matching CHEBI:61715. Applying it breaks r_0530 as currently written (heme o + NADH + O2 -> H2O + heme a + NAD), which balances ONLY because heme a carries the non-physical pair: with the corrected formula the equation is short one hydrogen and one negative charge. That is a real defect in r_0530, not a reason to keep the bad formula. r_0530 is annotated eccodes 1.18.1.6 (a ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase) and named `heme O monooxygenase`, but EC 1.17.99.9 says the oxygen comes from water and the step is an oxidation consuming two oxidizing equivalents, not an O2- and NADH-consuming monooxygenation; and as written the reaction lumps two successive hydroxylations plus a dehydration into one step. Whoever fixes the formula should fix the reaction in the same change, and should note that the correction propagates to r_4040, r_4598 and r_4780, which the pipeline closes by separate code rules.

WHAT THIS BUYS THE PIPELINE, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It closes `no_structure_available` for these three metabolites and moves them to `group_decomposition_failed`, which is a more honest reason but is not a price. Component contribution has no group for the Fe-porphyrin core, so no structure and no pKa ladder will ever price heme a through the default route. r_0530 therefore stays unpriced on this record alone.

WHAT A HUMAN STILL NEEDS TO DO. (1) Decide on the formula and charge correction and on r_0530's stoichiometry, and take it upstream to SysBioChalmers/yeast-GEM if it is confirmed, since BiGG's `Heme A C49H55FeN4O6` with charges [-6, -3, -2] is the shared root. (2) Accept that no measured or tabulated formation energy for heme a exists. Five searches found none; the measured numbers in the literature are midpoint potentials of heme a bound inside cytochrome c oxidase, Em,7 near 380 mV or 230 mV depending on the companion heme's redox state, which are protein-environment properties of a redox step and cannot price a formylation. Alberty's BasicBiochemData2 should be checked directly rather than through a web search before the absence is called final. (3) Choose a surrogate deliberately. The one worth testing, and it is an untested hypothesis, not a result: heme o and heme a are the same molecule differing by a single CH3 to CHO at C-8, so the transformed reaction energy of r_0530 may be estimable from a decomposable methyl-to-formyl analog pair, letting the undecomposable macrocycle cancel the way a conserved cofactor group does. That would price the REACTION without ever pricing either heme, and it must be validated against something measured before it is admitted. (4) If a formation energy is ever wanted for heme a itself, note that only a computed value is likely to be available, which under this project's admission rule is recorded as `computed` and stays out of the default route.
